answer.read: Edelstahl-Service Donautal holds the AS-14404 material at fixed prices until March 2027 (doc:20260706-70710-M1), yet it insists on an AS-14404 clause (doc:20260912-70710-P08, latest e-mail). It wants protection against later rises in the index rather than any windfall now. It has already agreed to our requested 90-day payment and 36 months. It dropped from €6.10 to €5.45 on our terms in one reply and is still open, not final. It asks for binding volume. Our order history at €5.45 (a1) anchors its current price as a ceiling. Its OTD (88 %) and rising ppm (sc:70710@2026Q3) weaken its position.
answer.message: Thank you for accepting the three-year term and ninety-day payment. Your material is covered at fixed prices well into the contract, and our recent orders were all placed at today's price level. Rather than a sliding clause, we propose one firm price for the full term, which gives both sides planning certainty for the volume we have forecast. Our term sheet reflects this.
answer.reason: o2 is the only selectable option other than E0. It costs us about €4.1k less than E0, and its price comes from the explicit-driver clause estimate. It removes the clause, so we carry no index-move or index-risk cost. Its material cover until March 2027 also means a firm price costs the supplier less than it claims. The supplier is still open, not at final offer, and is conceding fast. Accepting offer:70710-1 now would forgo roughly €70k against E0 or o2, so we counter. Citing a1 anchors the talks at the €5.45 order history.
